text: Ndị Igbo na-akpọ ya “eze ihe ọkụkụ”, na-emekwa ememe ya kwa afọ mgbe owuwe ihe ubi ruru. Kedu ihe ọkụkụ a?
gloss: The Igbo call it 'the king of crops' and celebrate it every year at harvest. Which crop? — Yam (ji): the New Yam festival (Iri ji / Ịwa ji).

text: Kedu aha ndị Igbo na-akpọ mmụọ nna nna anyị na-apụta n'ememe, kpuchie ihu ha?
gloss: What do the Igbo call the ancestral spirits who appear at festivals with covered faces? — Mmanwụ, the masquerades. Dibịa is a healer, Ozo a title, Ụmụada the lineage daughters.

text: Gịnị ka a na-adịghị etinye n'ofe nsala, nke mere a na-akpọ ya “ofe ọcha”?
gloss: What is left out of nsala soup, which is why it is called 'white soup'? — Palm oil: nsala is cooked without it (pepper, salt and fish all go in).

text: Mezue okwu ndị okenye: “Ilu bụ … e ji eri okwu.”
gloss: Complete the elders' saying: 'Proverbs are the ___ with which words are eaten.' — Mmanụ (palm oil): «Ilu bụ mmanụ e ji eri okwu», made famous by Achebe.

text: N'ezinaụlọ Igbo, a na-akpọ nwa nwaanyị mbụ “ada”. Kedu ihe a na-akpọ nwa nwoke mbụ?
gloss: In an Igbo family the first daughter is 'ada'. What is the first son called? — Ọkpara. Nwanne is sibling, ọgọ in-law, nwadiala a daughter's child.

text: N'ịgba nkwụ, gịnị ka nwaanyị a na-alụ na-ebu na-achọ di ya n'etiti ọha?
gloss: At the traditional wedding, what does the bride carry while searching for her husband in the crowd? — A cup of palm wine, which she gives him to drink.

text: Mgbe nwaanyị mụsịrị nwa, nne ya na-abịa nọrọ izu ole na ole na-elekọta ya. Kedu aha omenala a?
gloss: After a woman gives birth, her mother comes to stay for weeks to care for her. What is this custom? — Ọmụgwọ. Ịgụ aha is naming, ịkụ aka the first marriage visit, ịgba nkwụ the wedding.

text: Aba, obodo a ma ama maka ahịa Ariaria, dị na steeti gịnị?
gloss: Aba, the town famous for Ariaria market, is in which state? — Abia.

text: Otu onye na-akụzi bụ “onye nkụzi”. Kedu ka e si akpọ mmadụ ise na-akụzi?
gloss: One teacher is 'onye nkụzi'. How do you say five teachers? — Ndị nkụzi ise: Igbo nouns do not change for plural; 'onye' becomes 'ndị'.

text: Emeka nwere naịra puku abụọ, Ada nwere naịra puku atọ. Ego ole ka ha nwere ọnụ?
gloss: Emeka has two thousand naira, Ada three thousand. How much together? — ₦5,000: puku = thousand, 2 + 3. ₦6,000 traps those who multiply.

text: “Ụlọ akwụkwọ” bụ ebe a na-amụ akwụkwọ. Gịnị bụ “ụlọ ọgwụ”?
gloss: 'House of books' is a school. What is 'house of medicine'? — A hospital: ụlọ + ọgwụ, the way Igbo builds words for places.

text: N'oge udu mmiri, ndị mmadụ na-eri ọka a ṅara n'ọkụ ya na mkpụrụ osisi gịnị?
gloss: In the rainy season, people eat roasted corn with which fruit? — Ube (African pear): «ọka na ube» is the classic rainy-season pairing.

text: Mmanụ dị n'ite na-ere ọkụ n'ekwu. Kedu ihe kacha mma ị ga-eme?
gloss: Oil in a pot catches fire on the stove. What is the best thing to do? — Cover the pot: it starves the fire of air. Water makes burning oil explode.

text: Karama mmiri juru eju nwere ike ịgbawa na friza, n'ihi na mmiri, mgbe ọ na-aghọ ice,…
gloss: A full water bottle can burst in the freezer, because water, as it turns to ice... — expands (by about 9%).

text: N'egwuregwu football, gịnị ka a na-eji “VAR” eme?
options: Iji lee vidiyo nyochaa mkpebi onye ọkàikpe
Iji tụọ ikuku dị na bọọlụ
gloss: What is VAR used for in football? — Checking the referee's decisions on video (Video Assistant Referee).

text: Kedu ihe abụọ bụ isi ihe a na-eji eme mayonnaise?
gloss: What two main ingredients is mayonnaise made from? — Egg (yolk) and oil, whisked together with a little vinegar or lemon.

text: Ose na-agba gị ọkụ n'ọnụ. Kedu ihe ọṅụṅụ kacha ebelata ya?
gloss: Pepper is burning your mouth. Which drink soothes it best? — Milk: its fat and casein wash away capsaicin, which water and soda only spread.

text: Akụ, nke a na-eghe eghe rie, na-efepụta n'abalị mgbe gịnị?
gloss: Akụ, the winged termites people fry and eat, swarm out at night when? — After the first rains, when they leave the mound to found new colonies.

text: Gịnị ka ị na-eji n'ekwentị agụ “QR code”?
gloss: What part of a phone do you use to read a QR code? — The camera.

text: Gịnị bụ “OTP” ụlọ akụ na-ezitere gị mgbe ị na-akwụ ụgwọ n'ịntanetị?
gloss: What is the 'OTP' your bank texts you when you pay online? — A one-time password: a code valid for a single use.

text: Batrị ekwentị dị 60%, ọ na-ebelata 10% kwa awa. Awa ole ka ọ ga-ewe ka ọ gwụchaa?
gloss: A phone battery is at 60% and drops 10% an hour. How many hours until it is empty? — 6: 60 ÷ 10.

text: Na fim Disney “Frozen”, kedu nwanne nwaanyị nwere ike ime ka ihe niile ghọọ ice?
gloss: In Disney's 'Frozen', which sister can turn everything to ice? — Elsa. Anna is her sister; Moana and Ariel are other Disney heroines.

text: Nọmba ekwentị na-amalite na “+234” bụ nke mba gịnị?
gloss: A phone number starting with +234 belongs to which country? — Nigeria. Ghana is +233, Cameroon +237, Benin +229.

text: Na WhatsApp, gịnị na-egosi na onye ahụ agụọla ozi gị?
gloss: On WhatsApp, what shows that someone has read your message? — Two blue ticks. One grey tick is sent, two grey delivered.

text: Anthony Joshua, onye nne na nna ya si Naịjirịa, bụ onye mmeri ụwa n'egwuregwu gịnị?
gloss: Anthony Joshua, whose parents are Nigerian, became world champion in which sport? — Boxing (heavyweight).

text: N'akụkọ ifo Gris, onye fere nso anyanwụ n'nku e ji wax rapara, wee daa?
gloss: In Greek myth, who flew too close to the sun on wings stuck with wax, and fell? — Icarus.

text: Ọ bụrụ na aha egwu nwere “feat.” n'ime ya, gịnị ka ọ na-egosi?
options: Onye ọbụ abụ ọzọ so bụọ ya
Ọ bụ egwu ochie e megharịrị
gloss: If a song's title contains 'feat.', what does it show? — Another artist sings on it ('featuring'). Not a remake, an instrumental or a live recording.

text: Gịnị ka a na-etinye na ntụ ọka ka achịcha bilie, fụọ elu?
gloss: What is added to flour so that bread rises? — Yeast, whose gas puffs up the dough.

text: Fela Anikulapo-Kuti bụ onye malitere ụdị egwu gịnị?
gloss: Fela Anikulapo-Kuti pioneered which genre? — Afrobeat. Highlife came before him; jùjú and fuji are other Nigerian genres.

text: Otu football Naịjirịa nke Nwankwo Kanu so na ya meriri ọla edo Olympic n'afọ 1996. N'obodo gịnị?
gloss: Nigeria's football team, with Nwankwo Kanu, won Olympic gold in 1996. In which city? — Atlanta. Sydney 2000, Barcelona 1992, Seoul 1988.

text: Onye dere akwụkwọ akụkọ “Purple Hibiscus” (2003), nke e debere n'Enugu na Nsukka?
gloss: Who wrote the novel 'Purple Hibiscus' (2003), set in Enugu and Nsukka? — Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie, her first novel. All options are Igbo women novelists.

text: N'okpukpere ndị Igbo oge gboo, kedu arụsị nke égbè eluigwe na àmụ̀mà?
gloss: In traditional Igbo religion, which deity rules thunder and lightning? — Amadioha. Ala is the earth goddess, Agwụ the spirit of healers and diviners, Ikenga the cult of the right hand.

text: Nọmba akaụntụ ụlọ akụ ọ bụla na Naịjirịa (NUBAN) nwere ọnụọgụ ole?
gloss: How many digits does every Nigerian bank account number (NUBAN) have? — 10. 11 traps those thinking of the BVN or a phone number.

text: Kedu n'ime ndị a abụghị otu mkpụrụedemede n'abịdịị Igbo?
gloss: Which of these is not a single letter of the Igbo alphabet? — th. Gb, kp and nw are letters of the Ọnwụ alphabet; Igbo has no 'th' sound.

text: Ọgba Ogbunike, ebe a na-eyipụ akpụkpọ ụkwụ tupu a banye, dị na steeti gịnị?
gloss: Ogbunike Caves, where visitors take off their shoes before entering, are in which state? — Anambra (Oyi area).

text: Kedu ihe dị n'ọbara, nwere iron, na-ebu oxygen gaa n'ahụ niile?
gloss: What iron-containing substance in blood carries oxygen around the body? — Haemoglobin.

text: Ọwa mmiri Suez dị n'Ijipt jikọrọ Oké Osimiri Mediterenịan na…?
gloss: Egypt's Suez Canal links the Mediterranean with...? — The Red Sea. The Black, Caspian and Dead Seas are its neighbours on the map.

text: Kedu ụlọ ọrụ mepụtara igwe egwuregwu vidiyo PlayStation?
gloss: Which company makes the PlayStation games console? — Sony. Microsoft makes Xbox, Nintendo the Switch, Sega the Mega Drive.

text: Akpụkpọ ụkwụ bụ ₦10,000. Onye ahịa belatara ya pasent 20. Ego ole ka ị ga-akwụ?
gloss: Shoes cost ₦10,000 and the seller takes off 20%. How much do you pay? — ₦8,000. ₦2,000 is the discount itself; ₦9,800 subtracts 200.

text: Gịnị mere ọkụkọ ji eloda obere nkume?
options: Iji mee ka ọ dị arọ
gloss: Why do chickens swallow small stones? — To grind food in the gizzard: birds have no teeth.

text: N'adreesị weebụsaịtị, gịnị ka “s” dị na “https” na-egosi?
options: Na ọ bụ nke ụlọ akwụkwọ
gloss: In a website address, what does the 's' in 'https' indicate? — That it is secure (encrypted).

text: Na fim “Black Panther” (2018), kedu aha obodo T'Challa na-achị?
gloss: In 'Black Panther' (2018), what is the country T'Challa rules? — Wakanda. Zamunda is from 'Coming to America', Genovia from 'The Princess Diaries', Narnia from C. S. Lewis.

text: N'afọ gịnị ka Naịjirịa ji naịra na kobo dochie pound?
gloss: In what year did Nigeria replace the pound with the naira and kobo? — 1973 (1 January).

text: Kedu ihe ọkpụkpụ osisi nwere mpi, nke na-anọchite anya aka nri nwoke na mmeri ya?
gloss: Which carved wooden figure with horns stands for a man's right hand and his success? — Ikenga. Ọfọ is the staff of authority, ekwe the slit drum, okwa the kola bowl.

text: Onye ọbụ abụ highlife si Atani gụrụ egwu a ma ama “Osondi Owendi”?
gloss: Which highlife singer from Atani sang the famous 'Osondi Owendi'? — Chief Stephen Osita Osadebe.

text: Ego “cedi” bụ ego mba gịnị?
gloss: The cedi is the currency of which country? — Ghana. Gambia uses the dalasi, Sierra Leone the leone, Liberia the dollar.

text: Kedu afọ ka ọnụọgụ Rom “MMXX” na-egosi?
gloss: Which year do the Roman numerals MMXX show? — 2020: M = 1000 twice, X = 10 twice.

text: Kedu aha akara ederede oge gboo ndị Ejagham, Efik na ụfọdụ ndị Igbo jiri dee ihe?
gloss: What is the old sign-writing used by the Ejagham, Efik and some Igbo? — Nsibidi. Uli is body and wall painting, Ajami Arabic script for African languages, Tifinagh the Berber script.

text: A tọpụrụ nkume n'elu ụlọ elu. Ọ bụrụ na ikuku egbochighị ya, ihe dị ka ọsọ ole ka ọ ga-enwe mgbe sekọn 2 gachara?
gloss: A stone is dropped from a tall building. Ignoring air, about how fast is it falling after 2 seconds? — About 20 m/s: gravity adds about 9.8 m/s each second. 10 m/s is the one-second answer.

text: Afọ abụọ ka Wole Soyinka nwetasịrị Nobel akwụkwọ (1986), onye edemede Ijipt nwetara ya. Onye?
gloss: Two years after Wole Soyinka won the Nobel in literature (1986), an Egyptian writer won it. Who? — Naguib Mahfouz (1988). The others are major Egyptian writers who never won it.
